record_type_quote:
We used the extensive replication package provided by the authors on Github
(https://github.com/JanaLasser/new-ontology-of-truth/tree/main) and the data from the OSF
repository (https://osf.io/vny8k/overview).

targets.authors: Lasser, J., Aroyehun, S. T., Carrella, F., Simchon, A., Garcia, D., & Lewandowsky, S.
targets.title: From alternative conceptions of honesty to alternative facts in communications by US politicians.
targets.evidence_quote: We decided to replicate all claims made in the original article.
targets.outcome_computational_quote:
The two files “tweets_for_lme_modelling_NG.csv.gzip” and “tweets_for_lme_
modelling_independent.csv.gzip” were missing as well. They appear to have been deleted from the
OSF repository. These files are necessary for reproducing the linear mixed effects models that test the
association between belief-speaking and fact-speaking similarity, party affiliation, and trustworthiness
of linked articles.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote:
All robustness checks, without exception, confirm the stability of the original estimates.
Together, they suggest that the primary conclusions – that belief speaking and fact speaking
simultaneously increase – withstand variations in sampling, statistical power, and model specification,
reinforcing confidence in the reliability of the replicated findings.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Computational scope was initially all claims, and the central mixed-effects association between honesty language and source quality could not be run because required analysis data were missing. No comparable numbers emerged for that central analysis. Figure 2 and the temporal Welch tests did reproduce, so the computational classification has aggregation uncertainty: technical failure describes the blocked central model, not every output. Robustness was independently tested for the available temporal Welch findings only; all tested specifications confirmed them. Authors did not rerun after package updates.

reasoning: Original data/code reanalysis, not new-sample collection. Primary OSF PDF title and all four authors match assignment. One reference and target. Partial computational successes coexist with a blocked central association model; robustness conclusions apply only to temporal increases that could be tested.
